📖 Scientific Overview

STN7 and STN8 are paralogous serine/threonine protein kinases embedded in the chloroplast thylakoid membrane of Arabidopsis thaliana. Both face the chloroplast stroma with their catalytic kinase domains. Despite 36% sequence identity, they have evolved distinct substrate specificities and regulatory roles in light acclimation and photosystem maintenance.

STN7 (Q9S713)
Regulates state transitions via LHCII phosphorylation. Activated by reduced plastoquinone pool. Balances PSI/PSII excitation.
STN8 (Q9LZV4)
Regulates PSII repair cycle via core protein phosphorylation. Activated by high-light stress. Facilitates D1 turnover via FtsH.

Intracellular Signaling Pathway

11. High PSII illumination → PQ pool reduction
22. Cyt b6f complex senses reduced PQ → activates STN7
33. STN7 kinase domain phosphorylates LHCII Thr-5
44. Phospho-LHCII detaches from PSII (grana)
55. Phospho-LHCII migrates to stroma lamellae
66. Phospho-LHCII docks at PSI via PSI-H/PSI-L
77. PSI antenna size increases → balanced excitation
88. Reversed by TAP38/PPH1 phosphatase under State 1 conditions

Intracellular Signaling Pathway

11. High-light stress → excess photons at PSII → D1 photodamage
22. ROS/singlet oxygen signal activates STN8 kinase
33. STN8 phosphorylates D1 Thr-2, D2 Ser-2, CP43, PsbH
44. Phospho-PSII core destabilizes grana stacking
55. Damaged PSII migrates to stroma lamellae / grana margins
66. FtsH protease (Zn-metalloprotease) degrades phospho-D1
77. New D1 is inserted → PSII reassembly
88. PBCP phosphatase reverses remaining phosphorylation
99. Repaired PSII re-enters grana stacks
